name: Cookie Dough – GDPR Cookie Consent Banner & Google Consent Mode v2
author: Ludwig You

sections.description:
Cookie Dough is a cookie consent banner for WordPress that does what the law asks: nothing is loaded before your visitor says yes.

Most cookie notices only show a banner. Cookie Dough holds back Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, YouTube, Google Maps and the other trackers of your site until the visitor agrees, lets them refuse in one click, remembers the choice and keeps the proof. It follows the GDPR (RGPD), the ePrivacy directive and the CNIL guidelines on cookies, and it sends Google Consent Mode v2 signals out of the box.

Everything runs inside your WordPress: no account, no cloud service, no pageview limit, no data sent to us.

Why site owners pick Cookie Dough

  • Real blocking before consent. Scripts, iframes (YouTube, Vimeo, Google Maps…) and remote style sheets (Google Fonts…) of your declared services are neutralised on the server and switched on in the browser only after consent.
  • Works with page caches and CDNs. The page is the same for every visitor, so WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, Cloudflare and the others keep working.
  • Refusing is as easy as accepting. “Refuse all” sits next to “Accept all”, on the first screen, with the same look – the CNIL rule most banners still miss.
  • Choices purpose by purpose, service by service. Nothing is pre-ticked. Visitors can change their mind at any time from a floating button or a link in your footer.
  • Google Consent Mode v2 built in. ad_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization and analytics_storage start as “denied” and follow the choice, before any Google tag runs. A cdc_consent_update dataLayer event is there for Google Tag Manager.
  • A compliance score, not guesswork. The Compliance screen checks your configuration against the rules and fixes most points in one click.
  • Site scan. Cookie Dough reads your active plugins and your home page, finds the trackers and declares them for you. 28 popular services are recognised and blocked automatically; 250+ more are in the catalogue.
  • Consent register. Each choice is recorded with its date, a random consent ID and the version of your cookie list – your proof of consent. No IP address is stored.
  • Guided setup in about two minutes, then four ready-made designs with a live preview: card, bar or window, your colours, your texts.
  • Placeholders for blocked content. A blocked video or map is replaced by a tidy box that lets the visitor accept that service only.
  • Accessible. Keyboard navigation, focus management, screen reader labels and a contrast check. The banner lives in a shadow root, so your theme cannot break it.
  • Light. One small deferred script, one style sheet, no jQuery, no external request.

What is checked for you

  • Trackers found by the scan that are not declared (and therefore not blocked)
  • Services declared as “strictly necessary” that usually need consent
  • Refuse button as visible as the accept button
  • A way to withdraw consent on every page
  • How long the choice is remembered (6 months recommended by the CNIL, 13 months maximum)
  • Link to your privacy policy
  • Proof of consent, and a new consent when your list of services changes
  • Google Consent Mode v2 when Google tags are used
  • Readable colours (WCAG AA contrast)

Services recognised out of the box

Google Analytics (GA4), Google Tag Manager, Google Ads, Google AdSense, Google Maps, Google Fonts, Google reCAPTCHA, YouTube, Vimeo, Dailymotion, Meta Pixel (Facebook), Facebook social plugins, Instagram, X (Twitter), LinkedIn Insight Tag, TikTok Pixel, Pinterest Tag, Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar, Matomo, Jetpack Stats, HubSpot, Mailchimp, Crisp, Calendly, Stripe, WooCommerce and WordPress itself. Any other service can be added by hand: give it a name, a purpose and a piece of its address, or paste its code.

Made for

  • Site owners who want a cookie banner that is lawful without reading a legal treaty
  • WooCommerce shops that run Google Ads, Meta Pixel or analytics and need Consent Mode v2
  • Agencies and freelancers who want the same clean setup on every client site
  • Developers: type="text/plain" tags with data-cdc-category, a small JavaScript API (CookieDough.hasConsent(), CookieDough.on( 'consent' )), a PHP helper, filters and actions everywhere, and the WP Consent API

Shortcodes

  • [cookie_dough_preferences] – a “Cookie preferences” link for your footer
  • [cookie_dough_declaration] – the table of your services and cookies, for your privacy or cookie policy
  • [cookie_dough_consent] – the consent ID and the date of the visitor’s choice

Cookie Dough Pro

Everything that makes the banner lawful is free and stays free. The optional Cookie Dough Pro add-on goes further:

  • Whole-site scan (up to 30 pages), weekly, with an e-mail alert when a new tracker appears, and 45+ more recognised services
  • Consent register kept up to 36 months, search by consent ID, CSV export
  • Consent statistics day by day
  • 8 premium designs, your own images, custom CSS, banner without the credit line
  • Google Consent Mode v2 advanced mode, Meta Pixel, Microsoft UET and Clarity consent signals
  • Regional rules (banner only in the EU, EEA, UK and Switzerland), one choice shared across sub-domains
  • Cookie policy page generator, import / export of the configuration
  • AI assistants (MCP): let Claude or another assistant audit and fix a site

En français

Cookie Dough est un bandeau cookies RGPD pour WordPress conforme aux recommandations de la CNIL : aucun traceur n’est chargé avant le consentement, « Tout refuser » est aussi visible que « Tout accepter », le choix se fait finalité par finalité et la preuve du consentement est conservée. Google Consent Mode v2, scan du site, registre des consentements et score de conformité sont inclus, sans compte ni service externe. L’extension est traduite en français.

Privacy and transparency

  • The plugin makes no request to any third-party server.
  • The consent register stays in your own database and holds no IP address and no name.
  • The banner shows a small credit line, “Cookie Dough · powered by webdeclic”, with a link to webdeclic.com.
  • Cookie Dough helps you comply; it is not legal advice. You remain responsible for your privacy policy and for the services you use.

Other plugins by Webdeclic

Webdeclic is a French web agency based in Paris. We also make:

  • QuickWebP – Compress / Optimize Images & Convert WebP
  • Mentions Légales par Webdeclic
  • Universal Honey Pot
  • Clean My WP

⭐️ If Cookie Dough helps you, a 5-star review on WordPress.org helps us a lot.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins > Add New, search for “Cookie Dough” and click Install, then Activate. (Or upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.)
  2. The guided setup opens: let it scan your site, pick a design and confirm the recommended compliance options.
  3. Open your site in a private window to see the banner as your visitors do.
  4. Optional: add the [cookie_dough_preferences] shortcode to your footer and [cookie_dough_declaration] to your privacy policy.

Updating from version 2? Your texts, colours, floating button and services are converted automatically; nothing is deleted.
sections.faq:
Does Cookie Dough really block cookies before consent?

Yes. The scripts, iframes and style sheets of every service you declare (outside “strictly necessary”) are neutralised in the HTML before the page leaves your server. The banner script switches them on in the browser, only for what the visitor accepted. Refused or withdrawn services stay off, and their known cookies are deleted when consent is withdrawn.

Is Cookie Dough compliant with the GDPR / RGPD and the CNIL guidelines?

It is built around them: prior consent, refusal as easy as acceptance, no pre-ticked box, choice per purpose, easy withdrawal, a 6-month default before asking again, proof of consent, a new consent when the list of services changes. The Compliance screen tells you what is left to do on your site. A plugin cannot make a site compliant on its own: your privacy policy and the services you choose matter too.

Does it support Google Consent Mode v2?

Yes, natively and for free. The default state (“denied”) is sent at the very top of each page, and updated as soon as the visitor chooses. ad_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization, analytics_storage, functionality_storage and personalization_storage are covered. Google tags stay blocked until consent (basic mode); the advanced mode is part of Cookie Dough Pro.

Does it work with WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, Cloudflare or another page cache?

Yes. The HTML is identical for every visitor and the decision is made in the browser, so cached pages stay correct. Cookie Dough also tells optimisation plugins not to delay its own script.

Does it work with Google Tag Manager?

Yes. Declare Google Tag Manager as a service (the scan does it for you), keep Consent Mode on, and use the cdc_consent_update dataLayer event as a trigger for the tags that do not follow Consent Mode. Switch on “Always ask for every purpose” in the Services tab so that visitors can answer for the tags loaded by GTM.

Does it block YouTube videos and Google Maps?

Yes. Their iframes are held back and replaced by a placeholder that explains why, with a button to accept that service only.

Do I need an account or an API key? Is there a pageview limit?

No. There is no account, no licence key, no cloud dashboard and no limit on traffic or on the number of consents in the free plugin.

Cookie Dough vs Complianz: which one should I choose?

Complianz is a very complete solution with a long legal wizard and documents for many regions of the world. Cookie Dough takes a shorter road: a two-minute setup, a compliance score with one-click fixes, a banner that is blocking by default, and Consent Mode v2, the consent register and the site scan included in the free plugin. If you mainly need a lawful, good-looking banner for a European audience, Cookie Dough is the lighter choice; compare both on your own site.

Cookie Dough vs CookieYes, Cookiebot, Axeptio or Didomi?

Those are hosted consent platforms: the banner is managed from an online account and plans usually depend on your traffic or number of pages. Cookie Dough is a pure WordPress plugin: your configuration and your consent register stay in your own database, no script is loaded from a third-party server, and there is nothing to pay per pageview.

Cookie Dough vs Real Cookie Banner, Borlabs Cookie or GDPR Cookie Compliance?

They are WordPress plugins like Cookie Dough, each with its own approach. What sets Cookie Dough apart: refusal on the first screen with the same look as acceptance by default, a compliance score that names what is wrong, a cache-friendly blocker with no setting to tick, a banner isolated from your theme, and a free version without limits on services or consents.

Is it an alternative to Tarteaucitron?

Yes, for WordPress. You get the same idea (services switched on one by one after consent) with a visual setup, a site scan, a consent register and Consent Mode v2, without editing code.

How do visitors change or withdraw their consent?

From the floating button shown on every page, or from any link you create with the [cookie_dough_preferences] shortcode (for example in your footer). Withdrawing is one click, as the law requires.

How do I add a service that is not in the list?

In Cookie Dough > Services, click “Add a custom service”, give it a name and a purpose, then either type a piece of its address (for example example.com/tracker.js) so that Cookie Dough recognises its tags, or paste its code so that Cookie Dough prints it only after consent.

Where is the proof of consent stored, and for how long?

In a table of your own database: date, random consent ID, choices, version of the cookie list and page. No IP address, no user agent, no name. Lines are kept 30 days in the free plugin (up to 36 months with Cookie Dough Pro). Visitors find their consent ID at the bottom of the preferences window.

I am updating from version 2. Will I lose my settings?

No. Your texts, colours, floating button and services are converted the first time version 3 loads, and the old settings stay in the database as a backup. Visitors are asked once more, because version 3 no longer pre-ticks anything.

Is the banner accessible?

Yes: real buttons and links, keyboard navigation, focus kept inside the open window, labels for screen readers, reduced-motion support and a contrast check on your colours.

Can I translate or change the texts?

Every text of the banner can be changed in Cookie Dough > Texts. Leave a field empty to use the default text, which follows the language of your site. English and French are included.

Can I remove the “powered by webdeclic” line?

The credit line is part of the free plugin; the Cookie Dough Pro add-on has a switch to remove it.

Is it compatible with WooCommerce, Elementor, Divi and other builders?

Yes. The banner is not shown inside page-builder editors, WooCommerce cookies are declared as strictly necessary, and the banner is isolated from theme styles.

Does it respect Global Privacy Control (GPC)?

Yes, optionally: visitors whose browser sends the signal are treated as having refused until they decide otherwise.

I am a developer. How do I make my own script wait for consent?

Write it as <script type="text/plain" data-cdc-category="analytics">…</script> (categories: preferences, analytics, marketing), or use CookieDough.on( 'consent', callback ) and CookieDough.hasConsent( 'marketing' ) in JavaScript. Add data-cdc-ignore to a tag that must never be blocked.
sections.changelog:
3.0.0

  • New: rebuilt from the ground up around the GDPR, the ePrivacy directive and the CNIL guidelines.
  • New: every non-necessary service is blocked before consent (scripts, iframes, style sheets), with or without a page cache.
  • New: choices purpose by purpose and service by service, nothing pre-ticked, “Refuse all” next to “Accept all”.
  • New: Google Consent Mode v2, cdc_consent_update dataLayer event, WP Consent API.
  • New: consent register (proof of consent, no IP address).
  • New: compliance check with a score and one-click fixes.
  • New: site scan (active plugins and home page), 28 services recognised and blocked automatically.
  • New: guided setup, four ready-made designs, three layouts (card, bar, window), live preview on desktop and mobile.
  • New: placeholders for blocked videos and maps, Global Privacy Control, shortcodes [cookie_dough_preferences], [cookie_dough_declaration] and [cookie_dough_consent].
  • New: JavaScript API (CookieDough), PHP helper cdc_has_consent(), many filters and actions.
  • New: accessible banner isolated from the theme (shadow root), no jQuery.
  • Changed: settings of versions 1 and 2 are converted automatically and kept as a backup; visitors are asked once more.
  • Changed: custom images for the illustration and the floating button are now chosen with Cookie Dough Pro (images already set are kept).
  • Fixed: optional scripts could run before any choice when the cache mode was off.
  • Fixed: the “refuse” button of the mandatory step accepted everything.
  • Fixed: service icons were loaded from a third-party server before consent.

2.2.5

  • Fix problem when not required step is disabled.

2.2.4

  • Fix Undefined array key “REMOTE_ADDR” warning.

2.2.3

  • Fix translate for WP 6.7.
  • Better RGPD compliance.

2.2.0

  • Replace old options (in db) with one option for all.

2.1.0

  • Add filter for hide powered by.

2.0.0

  • Design evolution.

1.1.0

  • Added support for cache systems (beta).

1.0.1

  • Fix CSS for Elementor page builder.
